prompt.context_jp: 彼の口から何気なくこぼれた一言＿、店にいる全員の手を止めさせた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces this new, attention-grabbing remark.

feedback.correct_en: The 一言 is brand-new information that suddenly enters the scene and causes an effect — classic が for new/surprising subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 一言 as an already-established topic, which clashes with the sudden, newly-dropped remark. を is wrong because 一言 is the subject that causes the stopping, not the object.

contrast_examples.jp: その人 は 先生だ。
contrast_examples.en: As for that (already-known) person, he's a teacher.

prompt.context_jp: それほどに、その一言＿唐突で、しかも妙に確信に満ちていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The remark was just introduced in the previous line; now the narrator comments on it.

feedback.correct_en: The 一言 was just newly introduced with が in the previous sentence; now it is the established topic the narrator describes, so は.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using が again would make it feel re-introduced as new info, breaking the flow. も would wrongly imply 'this one too, in addition to another remark.'

contrast_examples.jp: 犬が来た。その犬は大きい。
contrast_examples.en: A dog came. That dog is big.
(It's that dog that is big — identifying.)

prompt.context_jp: 庭野＿ほとんど眠れないまま、いつもより早く家を出てきた。
prompt.prompt_en: The paragraph has shifted focus to Niwano — he is the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narrative continues with Niwano as the subject of discussion — a topical frame, so は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like Niwano is being newly identified or singled out among candidates, which doesn't fit this quiet continuation.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が家を出た？—庭野が出た。

prompt.context_jp: がらんとしたフロアに足を踏み入れると、すでに一つだけ明かりのついた席＿あった。
prompt.prompt_en: A seat is being newly discovered as Niwano enters.

feedback.correct_en: Existential 'there was ~' with newly-noticed items takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the seat was already known. に marks location, not the thing that exists.

contrast_examples.en: There's a book on the desk (newly noted).

contrast_examples.jp: その本は机の上にある。
contrast_examples.en: That book is on the desk (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「家を売るの＿私の仕事ですから。」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi defines what her job uniquely is.

feedback.correct_en: 'Selling houses — THAT is my job' — exhaustive identification pairing a nominalized clause with 私の仕事 uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reverse the information structure ('as for selling houses, it's my job') and sound off here where she is stressing her defining role. を is impossible with だ.

contrast_examples.en: This (and only this) is my house.
This, by the way, is my house.

prompt.context_jp: 「1つ目＿ 旗竿地に立っている 一軒家だ。」
prompt.prompt_en: The boss is listing property #1 (contrasting with #2 and #3 to come).

feedback.correct_en: Listing items in parallel ('As for #1 … as for #2 …') uses contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out #1 as the exhaustive answer to a question, which isn't the structure here. も would mean 'also #1,' which doesn't fit the opening of the list.

contrast_examples.jp: 一つ目は赤、二つ目は青。
contrast_examples.en: The first is red, the second is blue.
Which is red? — The first one is.

prompt.context_jp: 「担当＿ 布施さん。」
prompt.prompt_en: Assigning the person-in-charge role.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for the person in charge → Fuse-san.' This 'X は Y' pattern frames 担当 as the topic and names the filler.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mean 'the person in charge (and only that one) is Fuse,' which sounds like answering a quiz question rather than making an assignment.

contrast_examples.en: As for the president, that's him.

prompt.context_jp: 「フォローはしません 売る時＿ 私が売ります。」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi contrasts 'following up' with 'the moment of selling.'

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: she won't do follow-up, but WHEN it's time to sell, she will. 売る時は sets up that contrast with フォロー.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try to make 売る時 the subject, which doesn't match this adverbial time phrase. で would mean 'at/by the time of selling' and loses the contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 普段はしないが、今日はする。
contrast_examples.en: I usually don't, but today I will.
Today is the day I do it (identifying).

prompt.context_jp: 「この家は私＿売ります。」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi declares who, specifically, will sell this house.

feedback.correct_en: この家は sets the topic; 私が exhaustively identifies that it is she (not Adachi, not Fuse) who will sell it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would create two topics in one clause and lose the 'it's ME who sells' emphasis. 私も would mean 'me too,' implying others are also selling.

contrast_examples.en: This one — I'll do it (not anyone else).

prompt.context_jp: 「八戸さんじゃなく 庭野＿売りました。」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that singles out WHO actually sold it.

feedback.correct_en: After explicitly excluding Yahachi, 庭野が identifies Niwano as the sole seller — exhaustive が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 庭野は would make Niwano a general topic and lose the 'not X but Y' contrast. に would wrongly make him a target.

contrast_examples.jp: 兄じゃなく弟がやった。
contrast_examples.en: Not my older brother — my younger brother did it.
My brother did it (just stating about him).

prompt.context_jp: 「夫＿丸元物産の エネルギー第一本部に勤めていて 私立中学の娘が1人おります。」
prompt.prompt_en: The client is describing her husband as background info.

feedback.correct_en: She's giving a profile — '(as for) my husband, he works at…' — classic topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 夫が would sound like identifying who among candidates is her husband. を is grammatically impossible here.

contrast_examples.en: It's my father (not mother) who's the doctor.

prompt.context_jp: カウンターの中ではママのこころ＿グラスを磨き、その端には白洲美加の姿もあった。
prompt.prompt_en: The scene is being painted; Kokoro is newly introduced into the frame.

feedback.correct_en: Scene-setting narration describing what is visible uses が for newly-introduced actors.
feedback.incorrect_en: こころは would turn her into a pre-established topic, but this is a fresh scene description. を is already used for グラス.

contrast_examples.jp: 向こうで子どもが遊んでいる。
contrast_examples.en: Over there, children are playing (newly observed).

contrast_examples.jp: あの子どもは遊んでいる。

prompt.context_jp: 南向きの大きな窓からは、冬の柔らかな日差し＿リビングいっぱいに広がっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The sunlight is being newly observed spilling into the room.

feedback.correct_en: A sensory, newly-perceived subject in descriptive narration takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 日差しは would presuppose the sunlight as a known topic, which breaks the fresh-perception feel. に marks destination, not subject.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕＿ その話聞いたの 結婚した後だもんな。」
prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro contrasts himself (as hearer) with Niwano, who heard earlier.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the nominalized clause 'the one I heard it' (僕がその話聞いたの), the subject takes が. It also pinpoints who heard it late.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕は inside a relative/nominal clause describing when 'I' heard it sounds unnatural; は tends to float out to the main clause. 僕も would mean 'I too' and lose the contrast.

prompt.context_jp: 自分が知っていることを誰にも打ち明けずに胸にしまっておくべきなのか、彼＿迷っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Main-clause subject describing Niwano's internal state.

feedback.correct_en: The paragraph's established topic is Niwano; 彼は naturally continues that frame while introducing a comment about him.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼が would signal he is being newly identified among others — but the discourse has been about him for several sentences. に is a wrong case here.

contrast_examples.en: It was he who was troubled.

prompt.context_jp: 「よりにもよって 錦ヶ峰関ってのは ＿が悪過ぎます。」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the word that means 'bad omen / unlucky sign.'

feedback.correct_en: 験が悪い is a set phrase meaning 'inauspicious / bad omen,' explicitly glossed in the next line as 縁起が悪い.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気が悪い would mean 'in a bad mood' and doesn't fit a superstitious complaint. 腕が悪い means 'bad at a skill.'

contrast_examples.en: To be superstitious / seek good omens.

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ いえ そんなことは… ＿なことをお聞きしました。」
prompt.prompt_en: Niwano apologizes for asking something uncalled-for.

feedback.correct_en: 余計なこと = 'uncalled-for / unnecessary thing' — exactly what he regrets asking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大切 ('important') would be the opposite of an apology. 便利 ('convenient') makes no sense for a nosy question.

prompt.context_jp: 「売れてないですけど 住もう君 着てても＿ないんで 脱ぎに来ました！」
prompt.prompt_en: Kagimura reports the mascot costume isn't working.

feedback.correct_en: 効果がない = 'has no effect' — fits a sales tactic that isn't working.
feedback.incorrect_en: 関係ない means 'unrelated,' which would say the costume is irrelevant rather than ineffective. 原因 means 'cause' and doesn't fit the pattern.

prompt.context_jp: 「同じ重さであることを 今 その胸に＿なさい！」
prompt.prompt_en: Machi demands they engrave the lesson onto their hearts.

feedback.correct_en: 胸に刻む is a fixed idiom meaning 'etch into one's heart / never forget.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸に置く is not idiomatic for 'remember deeply.' 胸に押す isn't a standard collocation at all.

contrast_examples.en: Put one's hand on one's chest (reflect).

prompt.context_jp: 「じゃあ みんな 支度ができ次第 現地に向かってくれ。＿入れて よろしくな！」
prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro psyches the team up.

feedback.correct_en: 気合を入れる = 'psych oneself up / put in some fighting spirit' — the standard pep-talk phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気を入れる is not idiomatic (one says 元気を出す). 根性を入れる exists but is harsher/less common than 気合.

contrast_examples.en: Put in fighting spirit and go for it.

prompt.context_jp: 「とってもお似合いなのに 何で隠すの？ もっと＿としなさいよ。」
prompt.prompt_en: Majima tells the couple to stop hiding.

feedback.correct_en: 堂々とする = 'carry oneself with dignity / be unashamed' — fits 'don't hide, be proud.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 淡々 means 'calmly / indifferently,' which doesn't convey pride. 着々 means 'steadily (making progress)' and refers to work, not demeanor.

prompt.context_jp: 人を見下しがちだった物言いも、いつの間にか＿をひそめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The condescending tone had quietly faded away.

feedback.correct_en: 影をひそめる is a set idiom meaning 'to recede / fade from view.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 顔をひそめる is not standard (眉をひそめる = 'frown' exists). 声をひそめる means 'lower one's voice,' not 'disappear.'

prompt.context_jp: 「…という意味において ＿な存在だったもんなぁ。」
prompt.prompt_en: Yashiro teases Shirasu as a one-of-a-kind no-growth presence.

feedback.correct_en: 圧倒的な存在 = 'an overwhelming / unmatched presence' — the joke lands because she was overwhelmingly bad at growing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 消極的 ('passive') doesn't carry the 'unmatched' force. 標準的 ('standard') contradicts the joke that she was uniquely non-growing.

prompt.context_jp: Machi is asked how she sold a house so fast.
prompt.prompt_en: Which answer sounds most natural as a punchy self-definition?

choices.text: 家を売るのが私の仕事ですから。
私は家を売ることが仕事ですから。
家を売ることは私が仕事ですから。

feedback.correct_en: Putting 家を売るの at the front and marking it with が creates a crisp 'THAT is my job' effect — exactly Machi's signature line.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatical but reads as mild self-introduction, losing the punch. C is scrambled: 私が and 仕事 don't fit together this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は歌うのが仕事です。
contrast_examples.en: As for me, singing is my job.

prompt.context_jp: Machi walks in and claims the deal.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'I'm the one who'll sell this house'?

choices.text: この家は私が売ります。
この家が私は売ります。
私はこの家が売ります。

feedback.correct_en: は on the topic (この家) + が on the exhaustive subject (私) is the canonical frame for 'as for this house, I'll be the one to sell it.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps the particles and sounds broken. C makes 私 the topic and 家 the identifying subject, which contradicts the meaning (houses don't do the selling).

contrast_examples.en: I will do this problem (plain statement).

prompt.context_jp: Adachi politely declines Rusudo's offer of help.
prompt.prompt_en: Which decline sounds most natural in this polite workplace context?

choices.text: いえいえ そんな… ご迷惑掛けられないです。
いえいえ そんな… 迷惑をあげられないです。
いえいえ そんな… ご迷惑を貸せないです。

feedback.correct_en: 迷惑を掛ける ('cause trouble') is the standard collocation; its potential-negative form 迷惑を掛けられない politely declines imposing on someone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 迷惑をあげる and 迷惑を貸す are not real Japanese collocations — 迷惑 only pairs with 掛ける here.

contrast_examples.jp: ご迷惑をお掛けします。

contrast_examples.en: I don't want to be a bother.

prompt.context_jp: Explaining what 験が悪い means.
prompt.prompt_en: Which paraphrase sounds most natural?

choices.text: 縁起が悪いってことだよ。
縁起を悪いってことだよ。
縁起に悪いってことだよ。

feedback.correct_en: 縁起が悪い is the fixed form — subject-marking が with the i-adjective 悪い.
feedback.incorrect_en: 縁起を悪い and 縁起に悪い break the standard particle pattern for 'X is bad' adjectival predicates.

prompt.context_jp: Dori wants to love quietly without conflict.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural?

choices.text: 世間とは角を立てずに ひっそりと愛し合いたい。
世間とは角を建てずに ひっそりと愛し合いたい。
世間とは角を作らずに ひっそりと愛し合いたい。

feedback.correct_en: 角を立てる (lit. 'raise corners/edges') is the fixed idiom for 'cause friction'; its negative 角を立てずに means 'without causing a stir.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 角を建てる uses the wrong kanji/verb (建てる = build buildings). 角を作る is not idiomatic for interpersonal friction.

contrast_examples.en: A way of speaking that causes offense.
